liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Peggy-O** (1 review): Keith, Jerry, and Phil are explosive in their 1974 style during this song [21]
- **Cumberland Blues** (1 review): The reviewer enjoyed this version of Cumberland Blues, noting it does not disappoint [22]
- **Playin' In The Band** (1 review): The Playin' In The Band to Uncle John's Band sandwich is described as juicy [15]
- **Truckin'** (1 review): The jam after Truckin' is highlighted as a standout moment of the show [26]
- **Not Fade Away** (1 review): The Not Fade Away performance is cited as a highlight of the concert [26]
- A Slipknot doodle appears forty seconds into the second round of Playing [17]
- A Slipknot doodle appears forty seconds into the second round of Playing [18]

## The recordings

- **gd1974-06-30.akgd1000e.moore.berger.106027.flac24** (recommended): audience recording; 24 songs; 229 min; rated 4.67/5 by 3 [1]
- **gd74-06-30.moore.weiner.gdADT16.15537.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 24 songs; 226 min; rated 3.67/5 by 3 [3]. Said about its sound: The audience recording has an airy sound and generally good mix with little noise [20]
- **gd74-06-30.sbd.weiner.17814.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 24 songs; 206 min; rated 4.53/5 by 17 [4]
- **gd1974-06-30.mtx.haugh.97185.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 24 songs; 207 min; rated 5/5 by 2 [5]
- **gd1974-06-30.sbd.miller.96275.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 24 songs; 214 min; rated 4.2/5 by 10 [7]

## Around the show

- Jerry made Bobby laugh after the Gideon lyrics during the song [15]
- The band may have been tired by the end of the tour [16]
- Phil blew up stars just before a magical transition into Uncle John's Band [22]
- The second set is average, less hot than shows from June 18, 26, and 28 [16]
- The show is overshadowed by performances from June 18, 16, and 23 [21]
- The Slipknot theme here is less developed than the June 9, 1973 RFK version [25]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1974-06-30.akgd1000e.moore.berger.106027.flac24**: taped by Jerry Moore; transferred by Rob Berger; source: aud>akg d1000e's>sony tc-152sd (4)maxell ud-120's, dolby b [1]
- **gd74-06-30.moore.weiner.gdADT16.15537.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Jerry Moore; transferred by Mark Cohen; source: Audience Recording: AKG D-1000E mics [3]. Also: This was the reviewer's first live tape, acquired six months after the show; Recorded by Jerry Moore using two handheld AKG D-1000E mics and a Sony 152 deck [3][17]
- **gd74-06-30.sbd.weiner.17814.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [4]. Also: This was the reviewer's first live tape, acquired six months after the show [18]
- **gd1974-06-30.mtx.haugh.97185.flac16**: source: SBD AUD Matrix Mix (65%/SBD 35%/AUD) from SBD (shnID = 96275) Recording Info: SBD > Master Reel > CD and AUD (shnID = 15537) AudMC > DAT > WAV > SHN [5]. Also: Analog to DAT transfer by Mark Cohen in January 2003; DAT to SHN by Noah Weiner [5]
- **gd1974-06-30.sbd.miller.96275.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Master Reel -> CD [7]. Also: Charlie Miller handled all transfers and mastering for the soundboard source [7]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Thecdbunker: [Grateful Dead - Springfield Special ( 3 CD SET ) ( Soundboard from Civic center, Springfield, MA, USA, June 30th, 1974 )](https://thecdbunker.com/product/grateful-dead-springfield-special-3-cd-set-soundboard-from-civic-center-springfield-ma-usa-june-30th-1974/) [28]
